mainen_l5pc.reason: production dt=0.0125 ms / 2304 segments fails step_abs_hi.adaptation_index at 1 of 7 audit points; the other 12 conditioning features reproduce on all 7
mainen_l5pc.remediation: finer dt or mesh was measured and is not affordable at campaign scale; see docs/decisions

miyasho_purkinje.reason: no tested step converges. dt = 0.05 and 0.025 ms fail ap_amplitude_mV (agreement 0.40) on both the published 1,088-segment mesh and a 1,264-segment d_lambda mesh; 0.0125 ms still fails ap_amplitude_mV (0.60) and 0.00625 ms fails membrane_tau_ms (0.80) against a 0.003125 ms reference. The failing feature MOVES between steps, which is the signature of threshold-adjacent audit points rather than of an under-resolved integration
miyasho_purkinje.remediation: not simulated. Halving again would make the reference the production setting; the honest reading is that this model's prior samples include points where a feature sits on a discontinuity, which a finer step cannot fix

tzilivaki_fsbc.reason: step_abs_hi.mean_firing_rate_Hz reproduces on only 25-50% of audit points at dt = 0.05 and 0.025 ms, on both the published 9,875-segment mesh and the 4,096-segment d_lambda mesh. A fast-spiking cell at ~145 Hz puts one or two spikes per 400 ms window inside the tolerance, and the step needed to resolve them is finer than 0.0125 ms
tzilivaki_fsbc.remediation: a converged campaign would cost ~4 h per 256 samples at 0.00625 ms on this morphology; not affordable in this release. Adapter, mechanisms, calibration and the failing audit are retained so it can be resumed

ortner_snc_da.reason: no tested time step converges: step_abs_hi.ap_amplitude_mV fails on 1-2 of 7 prior points at dt = 0.025, 0.0125 AND 0.00625 ms, non-monotonically. Separately, its maximum rate of ~7.5 Hz gives <=3 spikes in the frozen 400 ms window, so ISI-derived conditioning features sit at their definitional floor (protocol_coverage='partial')
ortner_snc_da.remediation: not simulated at all; the adapter and its failing convergence audit are retained as the documented record
